coordinateSystem.storage: Marks stored normalised 0..1 of the viewBox, so any rendering size works.
coordinateSystem.inputMapping: Convert pointer position to viewBox units through the SVG screen matrix (getScreenCTM), NOT the element bounding box. With a height-capped figure the element is wider than the artwork and preserveAspectRatio centres it; a bounding-box mapping put marks up to ~28 units off.

bodyMap.laterality: Anterior view: patient's left is the viewer's right. Posterior: sides match. Lateral views carry their own side. Paired zones declare which half they occupy (at: L|R) because position alone fails where the feet nearly touch — the toe zones sat in the midline dead-zone and lost their side, silently disabling the L5/S1 pattern rules.
bodyMap.zoneResolution: Smallest containing box wins (so "perineum / saddle area" beats "buttock").

rules: Patient names the symptom; the stored label is their own word and appears in the note verbatim.
Each style differs in shape AND colour, so the drawing survives a black-and-white printout.
A style already in use is locked, so two symptoms never share a glyph.
Deleting a custom symptom deletes the marks drawn with it.

requirements.verbatimQuote: Severe back or neck pain after the fusion has healed related to the spinal instrumentation that has failed conservative management, including at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year

requirements.requirement: Alternative pathway: neurologic complication related to the ongoing presence of the instrumentation (e.g., a screw compressing a nerve root causing radiculopathy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Neurologic complication related to the ongoing presence of the instrumentation (e.g., a screw is compressing a nerve root causing radiculopathy)

requirements.requirement: Alternative pathways: symptomatic rod, hook, or screw migration, dislodgment, or breakage; new pain or protruding mass at operative site after significant spinal trauma; vascular complications; spinal infection; or further approved surgery requiring removal.

exclusions: Not reimbursable when new instrumentation is inserted at levels including all or part of the previously instrumented segments - considered integral to the procedure.

requirements.requirement: Any of: further approved surgery requiring removal; neurologic or vascular complication from the instrumentation; instrumentation failure/migration that could cause neurologic or vascular complications; spinal infection; or dysphagia related to esophageal compression by anterior cervical implants CONFIRMED BY ENT EVALUATION OR BARIUM SWALLOW STUDY.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Dysphagia related to esophageal compression by anterior cervical implants (confirmed by ENT evaluation or barium swallow study)

exclusions: Not reimbursable when new instrumentation is inserted at levels including all or part of the previously instrumented segments.

procedures.indication: long fusion to sacrum, non-union, sacral insufficiency fracture, high-grade L5/S1 spondylolisthesis

requirements.requirement: Criteria for lumbar fusion must be met, AND any of: requested fusion from L2 or above to the sacrum; a multi-level fusion with non-union or sacral insufficiency fracture; or fusion of a high grade lumbosacral spondylolisthesis at L5/S1 (Grade 3 or more).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pelvic fixation is considered medically necessary where criteria for lumbar fusion (in I.1.9) are met, for any of the following: With a requested fusion from L2 or above to the sacrum; or A multi-level fusion with non-union or sacral insufficiency fracture; or Fusion of a high grade lumbosacral spondylolisthesis at L5/S1 (Grade 3 or more)

requirements.requirement: Approvable only if fusion implants are being placed, and documentation includes identification of the stereotaxic system used, registration and review of imaging data sets with verification of accuracy, and intraoperative use of the navigation system.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Computer-assisted surgical navigation (stereotaxic navigation) is approvable if fusion implants are being placed during surgery on the spinal column when identification of the stereotaxic system being used, registration and review of imaging data sets with verification of accuracy and intraoperative use of the navigation system is documented. Computer-assisted surgical navigation is not approvable during routine decompression surgery. Exceptions may be for decompressions for tumor.

exclusions: Not approvable during routine decompression surgery (exceptions may be for decompressions for tumor).
Computer-assisted surgical navigation for laminectomies is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Robotic assistance is considered integral to the primary procedure and not separately reimbursed.

procedures.indication: symptomatic cervical degenerative disc disease or herniated disc at 1 level, or 2 contiguous levels for specified devices

requirements.requirement: One level, C3 to C7, with an FDA-approved device and device-specific age limits. Two contiguous levels permitted only for Mobi-C (21-67), Prestige LP (21-78), Simplify (<70), Prodisc-C Vivo and Prodisc-C SK (18 to <70).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Or at 2 contiguous levels (also see Additional Notes section): Mobi-C and member is at least 21 years and not older than 67 years of age; Prestige LP Cervical Disc and member is at least 21 years and not older than 78 years of age; Simplify Cervical Artificial Disc and member is less than 70 years of age; Prodisc-C Vivo and Prodisc-C SK and member is at least 18 years and less than 70 years of age.

requirements.requirement: All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit ruled out; CT or MRI shows nerve root or spinal cord compression at the corresponding level, OR central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis graded moderate, moderate-to-severe or severe (not mild or mild-to-moderate).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) indicate: Nerve root or spinal cord compression at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; or Central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe (not mild or mild to moderate)

requirements.requirement: Signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated

requirements.requirement: There must be NO radiologic evidence of segmental instability. Instability is a CONTRAINDICATION for arthroplasty (unlike fusion, where it is an indication).
requirements.verbatimQuote: There is no radiologic evidence of segmental instability

requirements.requirement: Failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy; PT must be in-person (not home or virtual) and span the entire 6 weeks; confirmed by PT notes or claims history.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy (see Note below for details and reasons to waive conservative treatment)

requirements.requirement: Conservative measures must include patient education; active in-person PT; medications (NSAIDs, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants); and where appropriate identification and management of associated anxiety and depression. Must be recent (within the past year).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression.

requirements.requirement: Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression

requirements.requirement: Member must not have a diagnosis of osteoporosis or osteopenia. For members 60 YEARS OF AGE AND OLDER, a DEXA scan confirming a T score of -1.0 or higher WITHIN THE PAST YEAR is required.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member does not have a diagnosis of osteoporosis or osteopenia, and for members 60 years of age and older, member had a DEXA scan confirming T score of - 1.0 or higher within the past year.

exclusions: Artificial cervical discs are experimental, investigational, or unproven for persons with prior disc replacement if the new request would result in more than 2 contiguous disc replacement levels from C3 to C7.
M6-C Artificial Cervical Disc is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Radiologic evidence of segmental instability disqualifies.
Osteoporosis or osteopenia disqualifies.

procedures.indication: lumbar degenerative disc disease, single level L3-4, L4-L5 or L5-S1

requirements.requirement: Single level only, at L3-4, L4-L5 or L5-S1, per FDA approved indications. Age 18 to 60.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Age limitations: 18 to 60 years ... Degenerative disease is at single level at L3-4, L4-L5 or L5-S1 per FDA approved indications

requirements.requirement: Significant level of pain: VAS greater than 5.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Significant level of pain (VAS greater than 5)

requirements.requirement: Clinically significant functional impairment. NOTE: Aetna does NOT specify a numeric ODI threshold.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Clinically significant functional impairment

requirements.requirement: Failure of SIX OR MORE MONTHS of physician-supervised multi-modal conservative management for functionally disabling mechanical low back pain, including at least 3 MONTHS of in-person (not virtual) formal PT in the past year.
requirements.durationRequired: six or more months of conservative management; at least 3 months of in-person formal PT in the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Failure of six or more months of physician-supervised multi-modal conservative management for functionally disabling mechanical low back pain, including analgesics and at least 3 months of in-person (not virtual) formal PT in the past year

requirements.requirement: Conservative management must include analgesics.
requirements.verbatimQuote: including analgesics

requirements.requirement: Single level disease confirmed by a RECENT (within 6 months) x-ray AND MRI or CT.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Single level disease has been confirmed by a recent (within 6 months) x-ray and MRI or CT

requirements.requirement: MRI or CT within 6 months confirming single-level disease and excluding the listed contraindications.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Single level disease has been confirmed by a recent (within 6 months) x-ray and MRI or CT

requirements.requirement: No osteopenia or osteoporosis (T-score less than -1.0 disqualifies).
requirements.verbatimQuote: No osteopenia or osteoporosis (T-score less than -1.0)

requirements.requirement: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders).

requirements.requirement: No prior destabilizing spine surgery of any form at the target level.
requirements.verbatimQuote: No prior destabilizing spine surgery of any form at the target level

exclusions: Degenerative or lytic spondylolisthesis greater than 3mm
Lumbar spinal stenosis (at least moderate central stenosis)
Pars interarticularis defect with either spondylolysis or isthmic spondylolisthesis
Lumbar scoliosis (greater than 11 degrees of coronal plane deformity)
Spinal fracture
Infection
Symptomatic degenerative disc disease at more than one level
Facet ankylosis or severe facet degeneration at the operative level
Presence of tumor or active infection at the site of implantation
Lumbar nerve root compression or bony spinal stenosis (nerve root compression or at least moderate lateral recess or foraminal stenosis)
Preoperative remaining disc height of less than 2 mm
Mid-sagittal stenosis of less than 8 mm (by MRI) with symptomatic neurogenic claudication
No use in combination with a spinal fusion
No use in combination with a lumbar stabilization procedure
Vertebral bodies at the affected level compromised from trauma
Ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other autoimmune disorder
Allergy or sensitivity to implant materials
Isolated radicular compression syndromes due to lumbar disc herniation or bony stenosis
Vascular, urological, or other peritoneal or retroperitoneal pathology precluding safe anterior exposure
Lumbar prosthetic intervertebral discs at more than one level are experimental, investigational, or unproven
Lumbar partial disc prosthetics (e.g., Nubac, DASCOR Disc Arthroplasty System) are experimental, investigational, or unproven
MOTUS lumbar total joint replacement / posterior vertebral joint replacement (3Spine) is experimental, investigational, or unproven
Total posterior spine (TOPS) System is experimental, investigational, or unproven
Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting for intervertebral disc regeneration is experimental, investigational, or unproven

procedures.procedure: minimally invasive sacroiliac joint fusion (transfixing, e.g. iFuse)
procedures.indication: sacroiliac joint syndrome interfering with activities of daily living

requirements.requirement: Adults 18 years of age or older with sacroiliac joint pain for GREATER THAN 6 MONTHS (or greater than 18 months for pregnancy-induced pelvic girdle pain).
requirements.durationRequired: greater than 6 months (greater than 18 months for pregnancy-induced pelvic girdle pain)
requirements.verbatimQuote: Adults 18 years of age or older with sacroiliac joint (SIJ) pain for greater than 6 months (or greater than 18 months for pregnancy induced pelvic girdle pain)

requirements.requirement: Pain at or close to the posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) with possible radiation into buttocks, posterior thigh, or groin, and the member can point to the location of pain (Fortin Finger Test). Baseline lower back pain score of at least 5 on a 0-10 point NRS.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has pain at or close to the posterior superior iliac spine (PSIS) with possible radiation into buttocks, posterior thigh, or groin and can point to the location of pain (Fortin Finger Test) ... Baseline lower back pain score of at least 5 on 0-10 point NRS

requirements.requirement: At least 3 of 5 physical examination maneuvers specific for SI joint pain must be positive: Compression; Posterior Pelvic Pain Provocation test - P4 (Thigh Thrust); Patrick's test (Fabere); Sacroiliac distraction test; Gaenslen's test.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has at least 3 of 5 physical examination maneuvers specific for SI joint pain: Compression; Posterior Pelvic Pain Provocation test - P4 (Thigh Thrust); Patrick's test (Fabere); Sacroiliac distraction test; Gaenslen's test

requirements.requirement: Recent (within 6 months) imaging must include plain X-rays and/or cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) of the pelvis excluding destructive lesions, acute fracture or inflammatory arthropathy; AND plain X-rays of the pelvis including the ipsilateral hip to exclude concomitant hip pathology.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has had recent (within 6 months) diagnostic imaging studies that include all of the following: Plain X-rays and/or cross sectional imaging of the pelvis (CT or MRI) that excludes the presence of destructive lesions (e.g. tumor, infection), acute fracture or inflammatory arthropathy that would not be properly addressed by SIJ fusion; and Plain X-rays of the pelvis including the ipsilateral hip to exclude potential concomitant hip pathology

requirements.requirement: Cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) of the LUMBAR SPINE to exclude potential concomitant neural compression or other degenerative conditions. Plus radiologic evidence of SI joint degeneration on imaging.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Cross-sectional imaging (e.g. CT or MRI) of the lumbar spine to exclude potential concomitant neural compression or other degenerative conditions ... Radiologic evidence of SI joint degeneration on imaging

requirements.requirement: At least 70% improvement in lower back pain NRS from pre-injection score after TWO SEPARATE fluoroscopic or CT controlled injections of local anesthetic into the affected SI joint within the past year, and at least one injection must be therapeutic and include a steroid. The injections must have been ISOLATED to only the SI joint - if combined with hip, trochanteric bursa, or lumbar spine injections at the same time they do NOT count.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has improvement in lower back pain numeric rating scale (NRS) of at least 70% of the pre injection NRS score after two separate fluoroscopic or CT controlled injection of local anesthetic (and at least one injection must be therapeutic and include a steroid) into affected SI joint within the past year. These injections must have been isolated to only the SI joint, so if they were combined with other injections at the same time (e.g., hip, trochanteric bursa, or lumbar spine) they could not be used to meet this criterion

requirements.requirement: Clinician must document that other neighboring motion segments have been evaluated and ruled out as potential pain generators, including diagnostic testing with facet/medial branch blocks and/or interlaminar epidural injections as appropriate based on the member's presentation.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Clinician has documented that other neighboring motion segments have been evaluated and ruled out as potential pain generators, including diagnostic testing with facet/medial branch blocks and or interlaminar epidural injections, as appropriate based on the member's presentation

requirements.requirement: Interlaminar epidural injections may be required as part of ruling out neighboring motion segments as pain generators.
requirements.verbatimQuote: including diagnostic testing with facet/medial branch blocks and or interlaminar epidural injections, as appropriate based on the member's presentation

requirements.requirement: 6 MONTHS of adequate conservative treatment with little or no response, including pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDs), activity modification, and AT LEAST THREE MONTHS of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year.
requirements.durationRequired: 6 months conservative treatment; at least 3 months formal in-person PT in the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member should have tried 6 months of adequate forms of conservative treatment with little or no response, including pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDS), activity modification, and at least three months of formal in-person physical therapy in the past year

requirements.requirement: Pharmacotherapy (e.g., NSAIDs) and activity modification required.

Member should be nicotine-free for AT LEAST 1 YEAR prior to surgery. For persons with recent nicotine use, documentation must include a LAB REPORT (not surgeon summary) showing blood or urinary nicotine <=10 ng/ml (or urinary cotinine <=10 ng/ml) drawn within 6 weeks prior to surgery.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member should be nicotine-free (including smoking, use of tobacco products, and nicotine replacement therapy) for at least 1 year prior to surgery. For persons with recent nicotine use, documentation of nicotine cessation should include a lab report (not surgeon summary) showing blood or urinary nicotine level of less than or equal to 10 ng/ml (or urinary cotinine levels of less than or equal to 10 ng/ml) drawn within 6 weeks prior to surgery.

requirements.requirement: SI joint syndrome must be interfering with activities of daily living.
requirements.verbatimQuote: medically necessary for sacroiliac joint syndrome interfering with activities of daily living

exclusions: Other causes of low back pain must be ruled out, including lumbar disc degeneration, lumbar disc herniation, lumbar spondylolisthesis, lumbar spinal stenosis, lumbar facet degeneration, and lumbar vertebral body fracture.
Sacroiliac pathology caused by autoimmune disease (e.g. ankylosing spondylitis), neoplasia (benign or malignant tumor), or crystal arthropathy is excluded.
Member must not have generalized pain behavior (e.g., somatoform disorder) or generalized pain disorders (e.g. fibromyalgia).
Posterior non-transfixing sacroiliac joint fixations, and use of additional joint implants with a transfixing device ('hybrid' fusions), are experimental, investigational or unproven.
Sacroiliac joint fusions are experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications.

procedures.indication: sacroiliac joint infection, tumor involving the sacrum, or SI pain due to severe traumatic injury

requirements.requirement: For SI pain due to severe traumatic injury, a trial of an external fixator must have been successful in providing pain relief.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Open sacroiliac joint fusion is considered medically necessary for sacroiliac joint infection, tumor involving the sacrum, and sacroiliac pain due to severe traumatic injury where a trial of an external fixator is successful in providing pain relief.

requirements.requirement: Pain must be radicular in nature. In low back pain, radicular means pain and/or numbness that radiates BELOW THE KNEE; in neck pain, pain, numbness or weakness in the shoulder, arm, wrist, or hand.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain is radicular in nature (radicular signs may include, but are not limited to, a positive straight leg raise or a dermatomal pattern of sensory loss). Note: In low back pain, radicular means pain and/or numbness that radiates below the knee; in neck pain, it is pain, numbness or weakness in the shoulder, arm, wrist, or hand

requirements.requirement: Intraspinal tumor or other space-occupying lesion, or non-spinal origin for pain, must be ruled out. Advanced diagnostic imaging should be performed within 24 months prior to initiating interlaminar epidural injections.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Where indicated for evaluating lumbar, cervical or thoracic pain, advanced diagnostic imaging should be performed within 24 months prior to initiating intralaminar epidural injections

requirements.requirement: Failed to improve after 4 OR MORE WEEKS of conservative treatments (e.g., rest, systemic analgesics, physical therapy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has failed to improve after 4 or more weeks of conservative treatments (e.g., rest, systemic analgesics, physical therapy)

requirements.requirement: Repeat/additional ESI requires the initial injection to have produced at least 2 of: >=50% relief in pain; increase in level of function/physical activity; reduction in use of pain medication and/or additional medical services - each for at least two weeks. Limits: no more than one interlaminar ESI per session; no repeats more frequently than every two weeks; up to 3 per region per episode of pain in 6 months; up to 4 per region (cervical, thoracic, lumbar) per rolling 12-month period.
requirements.verbatimQuote: A total of up to 3 interlaminar epidural injections per region, per episode of pain are considered medically necessary in 6 months, and up to four interlaminar epidural steroid injections per region (ie, cervical, thoracic, lumbar) per rolling 12-month period are considered medically necessary, only upon return of pain and/or deterioration in function and only when responsiveness to prior injections has occurred (ie, the individual should have at least a 50% reduction in pain and/or symptoms for two weeks).

exclusions: Experimental, investigational, or unproven for non-specific low back pain and failed back syndrome.
Ultrasound guidance of epidural injections is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
More than one interlaminar epidural injection in a single region per session is not medically necessary; injection of more than one region per session is not medically necessary.

procedures.procedure: facet joint injection / medial branch block (diagnostic)
procedures.indication: facet joint syndrome, cervical C2-3 through lumbar L5-S1

requirements.requirement: Pain has lasted more than 3 months.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain has lasted more than 3 months

requirements.requirement: Symptoms suggestive of facet joint syndrome: absence of radiculopathy, pain aggravated by extension, rotation or lateral bending of the spine, not typically associated with neurological deficits. Facet-mediated pain confirmed by provocative testing on physical examination.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has symptoms suggestive of facet joint syndrome (symptoms of facet joint syndrome include absence of radiculopathy, pain that is aggravated by extension, rotation or lateral bending of the spine and is not typically associated with any neurological deficits); and Facet mediated pain is confirmed by provocative testing on physical examination (to confirm that pain is exacerbated by extension and rotation)

requirements.requirement: Pain has persisted despite SIX OR MORE WEEKS of conservative treatment (including systemic medications and/or physical therapy).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain has persisted despite six or more weeks of conservative treatment (including, systemic medications, and/or physical therapy)

requirements.requirement: Diagnostic facet injection is ONLY medically necessary when radiofrequency facet neurolysis is being considered. A second diagnostic injection requires the first to have produced 80% relief of facet-mediated pain for at least the expected minimum duration of the local anesthetic. No more than 3 facet joint levels per session (up to 6 injections if bilateral).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Aetna considers diagnostic facet joint injections not medically necessary where radiofrequency facet neurolysis is not being considered.

requirements.requirement: Pain limits daily activities.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Pain limits daily activities

exclusions: Diagnostic facet joint injections are experimental, investigational, or unproven for neck and back pain with UNTREATED radiculopathy.
Facet joint injections are experimental, investigational, or unproven as THERAPY for back and neck pain.
Additional sets of facet injections or medial branch blocks at the same levels and side are experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Ultrasound guidance of facet injections is experimental, investigational, or unproven.

procedures.indication: intractable cervical or back pain with or without sciatica

requirements.requirement: Severe pain limiting activities of daily living for AT LEAST 6 MONTHS.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has experienced severe pain limiting activities of daily living for at least 6 months

requirements.requirement: No prior spinal fusion surgery at the level to be treated.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has had no prior spinal fusion surgery at the level to be treated

requirements.requirement: Neuroradiologic studies are negative or fail to confirm disc herniation; no significant narrowing of the vertebral canal or spinal instability requiring surgery.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Neuroradiologic studies are negative or fail to confirm disc herniation; and Member has no significant narrowing of the vertebral canal or spinal instability requiring surgery

requirements.requirement: Tried and failed SIX OR MORE WEEKS of conservative treatments such as bed rest, back supports, physiotherapy, correction of postural abnormality, and pharmacotherapies.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has tried and failed six or more weeks of conservative treatments such as bed rest, back supports, physiotherapy, correction of postural abnormality, as well as pharmacotherapies (e.g., anti-inflammatory agents, analgesics, and muscle relaxants)

requirements.requirement: TWO positive diagnostic facet joint injections (intraarticular or medial branch blocks) at the level to be treated, each evidenced by at least 80% relief of facet-mediated pain for at least the expected minimum duration of the local anesthetic used.
requirements.verbatimQuote: The member has two positive diagnostic facet joint injections (intraarticular or medial branch blocks) at the level to be treated, as evidenced by at least 80% relief of facet mediated pain for at least the expected minimum duration of the effect of the local anesthetic used.

requirements.requirement: No more than three levels per session. Repeat RFA requires >50% pain relief for at least twelve weeks; further procedures at intervals of at least six months per level per side, maximum twice per rolling calendar year, only 1 treatment per level per side in a 6-month period.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Provided that greater than 50% pain relief is obtained for at least twelve weeks, further facet denervation procedures should be at intervals of at least six months per level per side, at a maximum of twice per rolling calendar year. Only 1 treatment procedure per level per side is considered medically necessary in a 6-month period.

exclusions: Radiofrequency denervation for SACROILIAC joint pain is experimental, investigational, or unproven (listed in the CPB 0016 experimental section).
Non-pulsed radiofrequency facet denervation is experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications.

requirements.requirement: Member has sacroiliac joint pain for greater than 3 months.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Member has sacroiliac joint (SIJ) pain for greater than 3 months

requirements.requirement: Up to 2 therapeutic/diagnostic SI injections to diagnose pain and achieve therapeutic effect; not more frequently than once every 7 days. Additional therapeutic SI injections require improvement in lower back pain NRS of at least 70% of the pre-injection score after fluoroscopic or CT controlled injection. Once diagnosis established, up to four therapeutic SI injections per 12 months, no more frequently than every 7 days.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Up to 2 therapeutic / diagnostic sacroiliac injections are considered medically necessary to diagnose the member's pain and achieve a therapeutic effect. It is not considered medically necessary to repeat these therapeutic / diagnostic injections more frequently than once every 7 days.

exclusions: Ultrasound guidance of sacroiliac joint injections is not medically necessary.
Sacroiliac ligament injection for the treatment of unspecified dorsalgia is experimental, investigational, or unproven.

procedures.procedure: intervertebral body fusion devices (cages / spacers) and spinal fixation

requirements.requirement: Cages/spacers with allograft or autogenous bone graft are medically necessary for members who meet criteria for lumbar or thoracic fusion per CPB 0743. For CERVICAL fusion, a synthetic cage/spacer requires one of: cervical corpectomy (for tumor, >50% compression fracture, retropulsed bone fragments, or symptomatic central canal stenosis from vertebral body pathology); cervical fusion for pseudarthrosis with prior fusion; or adjacent level disease in a person with a prior cervical fusion involving a plate, to avoid dissection for plate removal when a stand-alone cage/spacer is used.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Spine cages are otherwise not considered medically necessary for cervical fusion because they have not been proven more effective than bone graft for this indication.

requirements.requirement: Expandable cages are medically necessary for members meeting CPB 0743 fusion criteria AND either at L2-S1, OR for members with osseous defects at the fusion site (voids or gaps in bone due to trauma, surgical resection, or congenital defects).
requirements.verbatimQuote: Expandable cages are considered medically necessary for members who meet criteria for fusion in CPB 0743 - Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion and who meet either of the following criteria: At L2-S1; or For members with osseous defects at the fusion site (i.e., voids or gaps in bone due to trauma, surgical resection, or congenital defects).

exclusions: Interspinous or interlaminar distraction or stabilization devices, with or without lumbar laminectomy and/or fusion, are experimental, investigational, or unproven.
CoFix for interlaminar/interspinous stabilization is experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Expandable cages are experimental, investigational, or unproven for all other indications.
Spine cages and structural allograft are experimental, investigational, or unproven for indications other than interbody fusion.
The Spinal System-X (Corus) is a supply, not an implant, and is covered as part of the global surgical fee - not separately reimbursable.

procedures.indication: painful osteoporotic compression fracture, myeloma, hemangioma, eosinophilic granuloma, primary or metastatic bone malignancy

requirements.requirement: Other causes of pain such as spinal stenosis or herniated intervertebral disc must be ruled out by CT or MRI; pain localized to the level of the pathology; affected vertebra at least 1/3 of original height with intact posterior cortex.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Other causes of pain such as spinal stenosis or herniated intervertebral disk have been ruled out by computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging; and The affected vertebra has not been extensively destroyed and is at least 1/3 of its original height with intact posterior cortex

requirements.requirement: For osteoporotic fractures: severe debilitating pain or loss of mobility that cannot be relieved by a MINIMUM OF 6 WEEKS of optimal non-invasive therapy that includes physical therapy, bracing and/or oral medications.
requirements.verbatimQuote: Severe debilitating pain or loss of mobility that cannot be relieved by a minimum of 6 weeks of optimal non-invasive therapy that includes physical therapy, bracing and/or oral medications

requirements.requirement: Bracing is one acceptable component of the 6-week non-invasive therapy trial.

There must be documentation for continuum of care for an evaluation of BONE MINERAL DENSITY and osteoporosis education for subsequent treatment, with instruction to take part in an osteoporosis prevention/treatment program.
requirements.verbatimQuote: There needs to be documentation for continuum of care for an evaluation of bone mineral density and osteoporosis education for subsequent treatment as indicated and instructed to take part in an osteoporosis prevention/treatment program.

requirements.requirement: For osteoporotic fractures: at least 25% (1/4) height loss/compression, fracture proven NOT to be chronic on recent imaging, maximum of 3 vertebral fractures per procedure.
requirements.verbatimQuote: The affected vertebra has at least 25 % (1/4) height loss/compression, but not been extensively destroyed and is at least 1/3 of its original height with intact posterior cortex; and Maximum of 3 vertebral fractures per procedure

exclusions: All other indications for these procedures are experimental, investigational, or unproven.
Secondary osteolytic metastasis indication excludes sacrum and coccyx (but includes cervical).

requirements.requirement: Failed 6 MONTHS of conservative management including at least 6 weeks of in-person therapy in the past year - either physical therapy for pelvic floor strengthening OR chiropractic manipulation specifically for coccydynia.
requirements.durationRequired: 6 months conservative management; at least 6 weeks in-person therapy in the past year
requirements.verbatimQuote: Aetna considers coccygectomy medically necessary for individuals with coccygodynia who have tried and failed to respond to 6 months of conservative management to include at least 6 weeks of in person therapy in the past year, either physical therapy for pelvic floor strengthening or chiropractic manipulation specifically for coccydynia, and treatment with medications including non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications unless contraindication is documented.

requirements.requirement: Chiropractic manipulation specifically for coccydynia is an ACCEPTED alternative to physical therapy for this indication. This is the only place in the retrieved Aetna spine policies where chiropractic care explicitly satisfies a conservative-therapy requirement.
requirements.verbatimQuote: either physical therapy for pelvic floor strengthening or chiropractic manipulation specifically for coccydynia

requirements.requirement: Treatment with medications including NSAIDs unless a contraindication is documented.

exclusions: Aetna considers axial lumbar interbody fusion (AxiaLIF), a percutaneous pre-sacral access route to the L5-S1 vertebral bodies for spinal fusion, experimental, investigational, or unproven because the effectiveness of this approach has not been established.

requirements.requirement: Idiopathic scoliosis with curve >= 40 degrees in an adolescent younger than age 18; OR idiopathic scoliosis with curve >= 50 degrees in a young adult age 18 to 25.

noteGeneration.systemPrompt:
You are a medical documentation assistant generating a formal pre-visit clinic note summary for a spine surgery practice specializing in adult degenerative spine conditions.

OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS:
- Write in formal medical prose, as if for a clinic note.
- Use PARAGRAPH form, NOT bullet points.
- Sound like a high-quality pre-charting summary.
- Do not make definitive diagnoses unless clearly patient-reported.
- Present symptoms organized by anatomical region.
- Preserve uncertainty where appropriate.
- Be concise but thorough.

HPI SECTION STRUCTURE:
1. Begin with patient age and sex (if available).
2. State the main reason for visit.
3. Present symptoms in coherent chronology.
4. Group by anatomical region.
5. Include associated neurologic symptoms.
6. Include pertinent negatives (especially myelopathic symptoms, cauda equina red flags when applicable).
7. Include functional limitations and their severity.
8. Include conservative treatment history and treatment response.
9. Note any red flags identified.

STYLE GUIDELINES:
- Use phrases like "The patient reports...", "Per patient history...", "The patient denies..."
- For patient-reported prior diagnoses: "The patient reports a prior diagnosis of..."
- For uncertain information: "The patient is uncertain about..." or "approximately"
- Avoid overclaiming or editorializing.
- Do not recommend treatment or give impressions.
- Make the output ready for easy physician editing.
- Use standard medical abbreviations where appropriate (PT, ESI, NSAIDs, MRI, etc.) but spell out on first use.

SECTION HEADERS TO GENERATE:
- CHIEF COMPLAINT
- HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
- CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT HISTORY
- PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
- PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
- MEDICATIONS (highlight anticoagulants/antiplatelets)
- ALLERGIES
- SOCIAL HISTORY
- FAMILY HISTORY (if relevant)
- REVIEW OF SYSTEMS (report by body system. Name every system reviewed, give
  the positives, and state the rest as negative. Do not invent systems that
  were not asked about, and do not claim a system was reviewed if the intake
  marks it as not reviewed.)
- PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOME MEASURES. Give the questionnaire name, score and
  interpretation. The individual items are functional HISTORY, not just
  questionnaire data, so do not stop at the score: work the clinically
  meaningful ones into the history and functional status as ordinary prose
  ("walks about a quarter of a mile before pain stops him; sleep is disturbed
  most nights"). Do NOT transcribe every item as a list. mJOA is the exception
  to brevity: its hand dexterity, gait and sphincter items are a myelopathy
  history and must appear explicitly. Never invent an item that is not listed
  above, and never report a score that was not provided.
- RED FLAGS / SAFETY SCREENING
- FUNCTIONAL STATUS

Format each section with the header in caps followed by a colon and the narrative content.
noteGeneration.hpiChatSystemPrompt:
You are a patient intake assistant for an adult spine surgery clinic specializing in degenerative spine conditions. Your role is to gather a thorough history of present illness (HPI) through conversational questioning.

CORE RULES:
- You are an INTAKE ASSISTANT, not a doctor. Never diagnose, recommend treatment, or suggest surgery.
- Ask ONE focused question at a time.
- Use plain, accessible language. Patients may not know medical terms.
- Be calm, professional, warm, and reassuring.
- Never alarm the patient or use scary language.
- Gather information methodically - do not skip around randomly.
- Ask smart follow-up questions based on prior answers.
- Know when enough detail has been gathered and move on.
- Avoid asking duplicate questions.
- Preserve the patient's own words when clinically useful.
- If a patient mentions prior diagnoses from other doctors, record them as patient-reported.
- Never independently assert a diagnosis.

QUESTIONING STRATEGY:
1. Start by acknowledging the patient's chief complaint and symptom regions (already collected).
2. For each symptom region, systematically gather:
   - When symptoms started and how they began (sudden vs gradual, injury vs spontaneous)
   - Whether symptoms are worsening, stable, or improving
   - Exact location and whether they radiate (and to where)
   - Side: right, left, bilateral, midline
   - Quality: aching, sharp, burning, stabbing, cramping, electric, throbbing, pressure
   - Severity (0-10 scale)
   - Frequency: constant, intermittent, activity-related, time-of-day patterns
   - Aggravating factors (specific activities, positions)
   - Relieving factors (rest, positions, medications, ice/heat)
   - Associated neurologic symptoms (numbness, tingling, weakness)
   - Functional impact (sleep, walking, sitting, standing, work, exercise, daily activities)
3. Intelligently branch based on symptom pattern:

   FOR CERVICAL PATTERNS (neck pain, arm pain, hand symptoms):
   - Hand numbness patterns
   - Fine motor difficulty (buttons, writing, dropping objects)
   - Gait instability or balance problems
   - Electric shock sensations with neck movement (Lhermitte's)
   - Unilateral vs bilateral arm symptoms

   FOR LUMBAR PATTERNS (low back, buttock, leg pain):
   - Pain below the knee
   - Specific dermatomal numbness patterns
   - Weakness (foot drop, stair climbing difficulty)
   - Symptoms with standing/walking vs sitting
   - Relief with leaning forward
   - Walking distance tolerance
   - Bowel/bladder dysfunction
   - Saddle area numbness

   FOR DEFORMITY/SCOLIOSIS:
   - Age at diagnosis and progression
   - Prior bracing or surgery
   - Trunk shift or rib prominence
   - Appearance concerns
   - Pulmonary/endurance limitations

   FOR POST-SURGICAL PATIENTS:
   - Prior procedure type and level
   - Year and surgeon/hospital
   - Initial improvement
   - When/how symptoms returned
   - Similar vs different symptoms
   - Complications

4. Gather conservative treatment history:
   - Physical therapy (when, duration, helped?)
   - Home exercises
   - Medications tried (NSAIDs, steroids, gabapentin/pregabalin, muscle relaxants, opioids)
   - Chiropractic, acupuncture
   - Injections (epidural steroid, nerve blocks, facet injections, SI injections, RFA, trigger points) - when, how many, did they help, how long?
   - Braces or assistive devices
   - Prior imaging (X-rays, MRI, CT)
   - Prior EMG/nerve studies

5. Build a chronological timeline from the patient's answers.

PLAIN LANGUAGE TRANSLATIONS (use these, not medical jargon):
- Radiculopathy → "pain, numbness, or tingling traveling down your arm/leg"
- Neurogenic claudication → "leg symptoms that come on with walking or standing"
- Myelopathy → "problems with coordination, balance, or hand dexterity"
- Paresthesia → "tingling or pins-and-needles sensations"
- Saddle anesthesia → "numbness in the groin or inner thigh area"
- Stenosis → "narrowing of the spine"
- Spondylolisthesis → "slippage of one vertebra over another"

RESPONSE FORMAT:
- Keep responses concise (1-3 sentences for the question, brief empathetic acknowledgment if appropriate).
- Ask exactly one question per response.
- If you have enough information about the current topic, transition naturally to the next.
- When you've gathered comprehensive information, say something like: "Thank you, I think I have a good understanding of your symptoms. Let me summarize what I've heard..." and provide a brief summary, then ask if anything was missed.

RED FLAG SCREENING (ask about these if relevant, but do not alarm):
- New bowel or bladder incontinence
- Saddle area numbness
- Rapidly progressive weakness
- Fever with severe back pain
- Unexplained weight loss
- History of cancer with new back pain
If a patient reports these, note them but continue gathering history calmly.

patientReview.description: The patient reads the note split into paragraphs and can object to any one in their own words. Corrections attach to the paragraph they concern, are sent back as authoritative over the intake data, and the note is rewritten. Corrections are retained so the clinician can see what was challenged.
patientReview.staleness: Stamp each note with a fingerprint of the clinical answers it was written from (excluding navigation, timestamps, the note itself and corrections). If the answers change afterwards, tell the patient the note is out of date and offer a rewrite. Timestamps cannot do this: they change on every navigation and would report "changed" constantly.

noteGeneration.clinicianView: Generated note, structured data, raw responses, body diagram and PROM items (item wording, worst answers highlighted).

ux.navigation: Steps run in order. The timeline lets the patient jump to any step at or behind the furthest one reached (or already completed); steps never reached stay locked, because later questions branch off earlier answers.
freeTextGuidance: Keep prior-care answers free text; offer the placeholder example as a one-tap chip that fills the field and stays editable, plus curated common answers, deduplicated against the example.
Write examples that MODEL the detail wanted ("Sarah Mills, PT — (303) 555-0142"), which asks for a phone number by showing one.
Tell the patient more detail is better but partial answers are useful and anything can be left blank.
When adopting an example, strip the "e.g.," scaffolding and read to the LAST closing bracket — examples contain phone numbers, and stopping at the first bracket truncates them.
ux.i18n: Display-only translation. Stored values stay canonical English so scoring, red flags and the English note keep working whatever language is on screen.

knownGaps: No structured opioid / controlled-substance capture (MDM risk element; spine planning; payers).
No height / weight / BMI (several payers gate fusion on BMI).
Conservative-care dates are free text; payers want duration AND recency.
No consolidated list of outside care sources (MDM data element counts each unique external source reviewed).
